A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same COIR benchmark. The complete main text, Appendices A–F, tables, figures, and equations are available for comparison; pagination changes do not represent missing material.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval evaluations, latency measurements, input-length experiments, and supplementary dataset evaluations in Tables 3–7.

after.justification: v3 retains the work's original retrieval evaluations, latency measurements, input-length experiments, and supplementary dataset evaluations in Tables 3–7.

M1.justification: COIR's dataset adaptations and evaluation pipeline remain unchanged, including embedding pooling and cosine-similarity ranking. The added Text-to-Code subsection heading labels an existing task rather than introducing a procedure.

E1.justification: Both retain the same ten COIR datasets, eight subtasks, and fourteen programming languages. The Human-eval, XcodeEval, and mbpp evaluations in Appendix Table 7 are also present in both.

E2.justification: The ten retrievers in Table 3 and the comparator subsets in the efficiency, input-length, BEIR-ranking, and Appendix Table 7 comparisons are unchanged. Newly cited works are not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Both report the same dataset splits, preprocessing, input limits, NDCG@10 metric, and latency protocol. Section 5.3 retains the same 512-versus-4096-token evaluation of GTE and BGE-M3.

E4.justification: The diversity, efficiency, input-length sensitivity, benchmark-ranking, and CodeSearchNet overfitting analyses are retained. Appendix A's dataset-difficulty screening and Table 7 evidence are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 3's score-distribution boxplots and accompanying variance discussion are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched results in Tables 3–7 and Figures 2–4 remain identical. For example, Table 3 reports mean NDCG@10 scores of 56.26 for Voyage-Code-002 and 55.18 for E5-Mistral in both versions.

T1.justification: Appendix C retains the same DCG, IDCG, NDCG, and weighted Jaccard definitions and mathematical explanations. No assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, conclusion, and Appendix F retain the same claims about COIR's novelty and coverage, existing models' retrieval difficulties and overfitting, and the promise of LLM-based retrievers.

C2.justification: Interpretations of specialization, generalization, resource tradeoffs, input-length effects, and overfitting are unchanged. Section 7 retains its English-only, multifaceted-search, and single-ground-truth-document limitations, while Appendix E retains the same applicability discussion.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 replaces the anonymous review repository link with the named CoIR-team/coir GitHub repository, changing documented code-access information. Implementation environments, model checkpoints, dataset links, and processing details otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds retrieval, RAG, and recommender-system citations, including MMDocIR and MC-indexing, and replaces the Mao et al. (2021) and Zhao et al. (2024) RAG references. COIR's positioning against existing code benchmarks remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds the missing '3.2.1 Main Task I: Text-to-Code Retrieval' heading and renumbers subsequent task subsections. The introductory application list expands slightly, while the main narrative and appendix organization remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures and table designs are retained, but placement and surrounding text reflow. Table 4 changes columns, Tables 10–11 become adjacent above Appendix F's continuation, and the closing sections no longer leave v2's nearly empty conclusion-only page.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves navigation and presentation by supplying the missing task heading and eliminating the nearly empty conclusion page. The named project repository also clarifies code-access information. These are limited usability gains; the scientific evidence, interpretations, and conclusions remain unchanged.
